summary: Specifies the Character Generator service, which sends data without regard to the input. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

plainLanguage.summary: The Character Generator service sends data without regard to what a client sends. A rotating character pattern can make it easier to notice missing or changed data while testing a connection.

questions: what is the character generator protocol
how does chargen work over udp
subtitle: Defines a test service that sends a stream or datagram of generated characters.

tldr.problem: A simple character-generating service can help people debug and measure network connections.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 19 sends a continuing character stream over TCP or, for each UDP request, one reply containing a random number of characters.
tldr.outcome: The RFC recommends recognizable output, including a rotating pattern of ASCII printing characters that can make missing or altered data noticeable.

today: RFC 864 is listed as an Internet Standard in the unit metadata. The metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: A Service for Testing Connections
sections.content:
A character generator sends data without regard to its input. The RFC describes it as a useful debugging and measurement tool for hosts that choose to implement it.

The data can be anything, though the memo recommends using a recognizable pattern.
sections.plainLanguage: The service sends generated data to help test a connection. The pattern can make errors easier to see.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Services
sections.content:
For TCP, a server listens on TCP port 19. After a connection opens, it sends a stream of data and discards received data until the user closes or aborts the connection. TCP flow control limits how quickly data is sent to the user.

For UDP, a server listens on UDP port 19. Each received datagram gets one reply containing a random number between 0 and 512 characters, and the request contents are ignored. The service keeps no state between replies.
sections.plainLanguage: TCP provides a stream that continues until the user ends the connection. UDP returns one independently sized response for each datagram and keeps no record between responses.

sections.title: A Rotating Character Pattern
sections.content:
One suggested pattern uses lines of 72 ASCII printing characters. The 95 printing characters are placed in order and treated as a ring, so character 0 follows character 94.

Each new line begins one character later than the previous line, wrapping around at the end of the sequence. Lines end with carriage return and line feed.
sections.plainLanguage: Each line starts one character later than the line before it and wraps around at the end. If data is missing or changed, the repeated pattern can look different.
